About us
Our School
Underhill School and Children's Centre gives positive ambition and power to the children and families of this community. We have a learning method that gives our children the skills and confidence to progress in the curriculum and pursue their talents both in and outside of the school day, and enables their families to support them in this. It is a school with brilliant opportunities created by a team of very special people who work together to make amazing things happen for this community.
Our values and ethos - The Underhill Way
Our school values and ethos have been developed to build on all the positives from the past and to take the school into the future so that we are preparing all our children for life beyond primary school. Our values incorporate the skills and attributes needed to be a success in the 21st century. We call this the Underhill Way.
Our team
We have a fantastic staff team at Underhill School and Children’s Centre who are all committed to providing the best opportunities our pupils and families.
Our community
We are a community with a rich variety of home languages, cultures, faiths and traditions and this is highly valued and celebrated both in the curriculum and in school life. Together with the Children's Centre, we provide a wide range of services and support for our families and the wider community.
Parents as Partners
We believe that parental partnership is vital to ensuring the well being and academic success of pupils. Parents are an essential component of our school community. We welcome parents to come into the school to support the children in their learning. Our PTA hold events throughout the year in order to help raise money to further enrich activities within the school. The governors also work effectively with the school to ensure the best possible provision and outcomes for its pupils. You can find out more about the work of the PTA on the governors page and the PTA section of the homepage
Contact us
Hopefully this website will answer many of the questions you may have about the school, but if you have anything further you wish to discuss please don’t hesitate to contact us.​
Jennie Reed and Nicola Hayles

Early Years foundation stage (EYFS)
our Early YEarS: Nursery and Reception
We are very proud of our Early Years: it really is a wonderful place for your child to take their first steps at school and into the big, wide world! We are very lucky to have a fabulous Nursery provision, where we take children from 2 years old, along with our fantastic Reception classes. Our skilled EYFS practitioners ensure that our EYFS is an incredibly nurturing place, where children feel safe and happy, and make great progress in their learning.
We offer a choice of nursery sessions for our 2, 3 and 4 year olds. If your child is entitled to 30 hours you can choose to take your daily 6 hours free entitlement in one block or you can choose to pay to have your child here for longer. We also offer breakfast and after school clubs for all children aged 3 or above. There are no financial barriers for families being able to access the Government funded entitlements
Please have a read of the presentation below for an outline of how our EYFS works, and there is photo gallery below that where you can see our EYFS in action and the fantastic spaces our children have to play and learn in.
If you are interested in finding out more, please do come and visit! You can arrange an appointment by calling the school office on 0208 449 2423.
Welcome to the EYFS at Underhill
What is the EYFS?
What kind of activities happen each day?
Our Curriculum Aims
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) is the time in a child’s life from birth to the end of the Reception year. It is based on the recognition that young children learn best through play and active learning.
Our Curriculum Aims
What kind of activities happen each day?
Our Curriculum Aims
Spark their curiosity and imagination (Be Curious)
Make them lifelong readers
Build on their physical and mental fitness
What kind of activities happen each day?
What kind of activities happen each day?
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Our days in Nursery and Reception are always packed full of learning and fun. The children have the opportunity to work with adults and their friends as a class, in groups or independently. Each day follows a clear routine to ensure the children feel safe and secure, and know what to expect each day. Activities and learning include:
● Start the day activities ●5 a Day dance ●Snack time ●Writing time ●Indoor and Outdoor Play every morning and afternoon ●Maths time ●Everyone Reading in Class ●Curriculum learning time such as Understanding the World, RE, Music, Art and Computing ●Storytime ●PE
The children have opportunity to play and learn in the role play, sand and water areas, small and large construction areas, the message centre, our book corners, the climbing frame, digging areas and to use outdoor equipment such as bikes, balls and hoops .
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
At Underhill, in both Nursery and Reception, we support all the children to be happy and friendly people who can understand and regulate their feelings and emotions; manage and regulate their behaviour on their own; make lots of friends and build positive relationships outside of the home.
Our nurturing and safe provision gives the children the opportunity to explore, take risks and develop their confidence and self esteem so that they are ready for the next stage of their learning journey.
Communication and Language
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Communication and Language
Oracy and communication is at the heart of our curriculum. We make sure that children are developing their listening, attention, speaking and storytelling skills. In our Nursery and Reception, they become happy confident communicators, able to express themselves in a range of ways with the vocabulary they need to move on to the next stage of their learning in Reception or year 1.
Physical Development
Personal, Social and Emotional Development
Communication and Language
Your child with develop the ability to run, jump, hop, skip, balance, climb, move and play with skill and confidence in our wonderful setting. We also have specialist PE teachers who deliver weekly lessons to all the children in Nursery and Reception.
Through drawing, painting, cutting, sticking, modelling and making, and building, they develop their fine motor skills so they can write and perform more ‘fiddly’ tasks with confidence.
Reading and Writing
Mathematical Development
Mathematical Development
All children that come to Underhill learn to love reading! We have a very comprehensive system for developing early reading skills. Along with the robust teaching of phonics, with reading books closely matched to their reading level, we have a wonderful range of books in all our class book corners and school library. The children visit the school library each week to borrow their own special book to take home. Learning is built around stories and story telling to ensure that they foster a passion for reading. We also love parents to come in a visit at story time and be a Mystery reader!
Through their play and learning, the children build their expert writing skills. We always write for a purpose in play and in guided sessions, or at each class message centre. The children develop their mark making and handwriting skills through drawing, modelling and making, climbing, and building.
Mathematical Development
Mathematical Development
Mathematical Development
Number, shapes and pattern are all around and we ensure that our provision both indoors and out, helps our children to develop a confident and concrete mathematical understanding.
Maths isn’t just about counting. We want our children to be to able notice patterns, to use mathematical language, to problem solve and reason. Through our provision and support, we make sure that all our children have the knowledge and number facts they need for their next stage of learning be that in Reception or year 1.
Maths is fun and we want to eliminate the ‘I can’t do maths’ concept that many people have!
Understanding the World
Mathematical Development
Expressive Arts and Design
Through learning about the past and present, different people and communities and the natural world, we build the historians, geographers and scientists of the future.
In our setting we have visitors and experiences that bring the wider world to Underhill, building on what the children know already and introducing them to exciting new concepts and experiences.
Our wonderful provision gives us the space and resources to learn about the natural world. We have different gardening areas and Nursery work with a local gardening group called GROW.
Expressive Arts and Design
Expressive Arts and Design
Expressive Arts and Design
Our team ensure that we foster your child’s imagination, taking exciting learning adventures everyday!
We have a wealth of resources available everyday so your child has the opportunity to draw, paint, make and create. Through planned activities and in their play, the children learn an exciting range of art and design skills and knowledge to enable them to express their ideas and imagination.
We love music and dance and to perform!
Monitoring Progress
Expressive Arts and Design
Monitoring Progress
Every day, we observe your child to find out their interests, strengths and what they can do. This helps us to plan their next steps. We share this information with you through SeeSaw (our online journal) and through meetings together.
Each of the 7 areas of learning has its own set of Early Learning Goals which determine what most children are expected to achieve by the end of Reception Class.
At the end of the school year, we share the children final assessments with you and their new Reception or Year 1 teacher.
Come for a visit!

You can make an appointment to come and visit through the school office and we run tours all year round. Please call us on 0208 449 2423.

curriculum Overview
our Curriculum Aims
●Broaden the children’s understanding of the world. (Be Caring)
●Spark their curiosity and imagination (Be Curious)
●Teach the children how to work collaboratively (Be Cooperative)
●Prepare them for life after Underhill (Be Confident)
●Make them lifelong readers
●Increase and improve their oracy skills
●Build on their physical and mental fitness
What are we learning at Underhill?
There is always lots of exciting learning happening each day at Underhill. In the morning, the children focus on English and Maths and in the afternoon, the children learn the other foundation subjects. There are also lots of trips and experiences to enrich the children's learning along with special days, where we celebrate or mark religious festivals and other important days and events.
Religious Education
Parents and carers have the right to withdraw their child from all or part of Religious Education (RE), without giving a reason. To exercise this right, please contact the Co-Headteachers through the school office, specifying whether you wish to withdraw your child from all RE or particular parts. We will respect your decision and make appropriate arrangements for your child’s supervision during these lessons. If you would like to discuss the RE curriculum before making a decision, we would be happy to do so.
Subject Overviews
English
At Underhill School we want our children to love reading and this is at the heart of our reading curriculum. We want all our children to be enthusiastic readers who read widely and frequently and take true pleasure in reading.
Maths
Get guidance to help your child with addition, subtraction, multiplication and division and find National Curriculum objectives for each year group with prompt sheets to explain some of the objectives.
PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education)
We deliver our comprehensive PSHE curriculum under three areas: relationships education, health education and living in the wider world. We aim to produce confident individuals who know and understand how to live safe, happy, healthy, fulfilling lives.
Language and Communication
Being a confident communicator is essential and at Underhill, we ensure that there are lots of opportunities for children to develop their speaking and listening skills through their play and learning.
Music
Our Music Development plan can be found in the documents section at the end of this page
Other subject areas
The long term curriculum maps for each year group can be found below or follow the yellow button to find out about each of the subjects and what the children are learning in each across the school.
If you wish to find out any more about our curriculum please speak to your child's class teacher or contact the school office.
Long Term Year Group Curriculum Maps
Home Learning
FRED - Families Reading Every Day
We want all children to be confident, fluent readers so reading everyday is a must. Our aim is for all our children to be reading for at least 15 minutes everyday.
When children are developing their reading skills and fluency, we ask them to read the book assigned to them by their teacher and as they develop their fluency, they can choose the books they want to read for pleasure. When your child has completed their reading each day, they tick their Fred Book mark and bring it to school each day to show their teacher.
Homework
Each week, your child will be assigned homework on a Friday to completed in their homework book and brought back to school on a Wednesday for the teacher to acknowledge. The homework tasks will be shared with you on either Seesaw (EYFS and KS1) or Google Classroom (KS2)
The homework will include weekly spellings, phonics, maths, reading comprehension and grammar, and are based on what your child has been learning in school that week.
Support Home Learning
Underhill School has been offered free KS2 learning and 11+ support to primary school children who are eligible for Pupil Premium. Eligible students will receive access to Atom Home for free (normally £575.90 a year).
Atom Home is an online learning and exam preparation platform for ages 7-11.Covering English, maths, verbal reasoning and non-verbal reasoning, children can practise 11+ questions and explore learning resources, mock tests, video tutorials, and exam preparation materials.It is a viable, more child-centric alternative to private tuition that we believe is a non-stressful and enjoyable way of making progress at KS2 and, when relevant, preparing for exams.
Pupil Premium Eligibility: You can sign up for your free Atom account by clicking on the ATOM Learning image.
After completing the form on the website, the school will receive a notification to verify your pupil premium eligibility and once that is confirmed, your Atom Home account will be created.
Non-pupil Premium: In addition, there is a 5-day free trial of Atom available for non-PP families and you can also use the discount code: Underhill20 to receive 20% off your first month’s payment.
Do you know someone who is eligible?
If you know someone whose child is preparing for the 11+, or is in need of extra Key Stage 2 learning support (they do not need to be attending Underhill), please do share the above link with them:
If you would like to find out more about Atom Learning or have any questions, please email pupilpremium@atomlearning.com and they will be happy to help you.

Inclusion at Underhill
At our school, we are committed to providing a quality education that prepares every child for success in their future. We aim to create a safe and supportive learning environment, where students can thrive both academically and personally. We offer a wide range of programs and extracurricular activities to help students explore their interests and develop their skills. We believe that every student has the potential to achieve great things, and we are here to help them reach their goals.
Our Inclusion team are available to meet with you to discuss any SEND, inclusion or safeguarding issues or concerns you may have. Please call the office and they will be able to put you in touch.
Jane Wood - Designated Safeguarding Lead
Joel Long - Learning Mentor
Kate Woods - Attendance and Medical Officer

Protected Characteristics
Protected Characteristics
Protected characteristics: (Gender, Race, Disability, Religion or Belief, Sexual Orientation, Gender reassignment and Pregnancy or Maternity)
Through our curriculum and in particular our PSHE and RE curriculums, the children learn about the similar and differences between us all and the importance of respecting everyone. The children learn that some groups are discriminated against and because of this there are laws to protect everybody's rights.
I can You can We can
Protected Characteristics
Protected Characteristics
Our values teach us that we can all achieve and we all should be included. Through our BE Words (Caring, Confidence, Curious and Cooperative), which are woven through our curriculum and school day, the children learn the skills of caring, confidence, curiosity and co-operation. We focus on our Be Words, thinking about them in our assemblies and recognise where the children are demonstrating our values.
Our Curriculum
Protected Characteristics
In the Classroom
We work to make sure that all the children are represented in our curriculum. We read books by authors from a wide range of backgrounds; we learn about different cultures and religions and their contribution to society; we celebrate and commemorate special events throughout the year; we have visitors such as Hope not Hate that teach and empower the children to understand what discrimination is and their role in preventing it.

In the Classroom
In the Classroom
We employ a wide range of strategies to ensure that all children are able to access the learning across the curriculum. We work with outside agencies to support us with this to ensure that all the children are getting the correct support and challenge.

Enrichment
We enrich our curriculum with trips, focus days and special events throughout the year. We make sure that all children have access to all the clubs we run, and work with external clubs to ensure that all children can attend the clubs that they want to. Extra adults are available to ensure that children with disabilities or SEND are welcomed and encouraged to attend clubs. We want all the children to take part in enrichment activities in order to find their spark!
You can find out more about our clubs here:
https://underhillschool.co.uk/school-clubs

Enrichment
Sport is for all. Everyone can join in. We have a huge range of sports opportunities available for children at playtimes and lunchtimes, through our curriculum and in the many tournaments that we compete in. Our SEND children attend Barnet LA Sports events and sports days. There is equal parity in our teams for girls and boys.

12.12.25 Christmas fun in Reception!
Beech class have created a wonderful 'Dazzling Door for December' by decorating paper plate templates covered with sticky back plastic. They chose different circular confetti shapes in a variety of colours and placed them on the sticky surface. The children loved doing this and were really focused on creating their own colourful patterns with a sprinkle of glitter on the top too to finish off the effect! This activity supports their physical development as they manipulate the art resources using their fine motor skills. We are very proud of our door, we hope you are dazzled too!
5.12.25 Christmas fun in Nursery!
28.11.25 Reception make Autumn wreaths
12.12.25 Christmas fun in Reception!
Conker class have been getting ready for Christmas this week. The cheeky elf has made an appearance and has been sent to the thinking chair several times!! The elf has not been following the class rules and one day he threw all the crayons on the floor. The children were very disappointed with his behaviour. We had a lot of fun making our Christmas door. The children wanted to make a Christmas tree and we decided to make our own Christmas tree using handprints. In Reception this week we have been looking at ourselves in the mirror and then using skin toned paint sticks to create our own self portraits. We are discovering that we all look very different but that we are all very special!
09.10.26 Gingerbread Man came to nursery!
This week, we have been reading The Gingerbread Man. The children particularly enjoyed the part of the story where the fox eats the Gingerbread Man. This led us to wonder: Why can’t the Gingerbread Man go into the water? The children shared their ideas. One child said, “Because he will get soggy,” while another thought, “He might melt.” To investigate their ideas, we each had a gingerbread biscuit to explore using our senses. We smelt it, touched it and tasted it, describing what we noticed. We then used pipettes to carefully add water to our biscuits. We noticed that we needed to add lots of water because it was quickly being absorbed into the biscuit. We continued adding water and watching carefully until the biscuits became very soggy. Eventually, they became so wet that they disintegrated and fell apart. The children really enjoyed this hands-on investigation and were able to see for themselves what happens to a gingerbread biscuit when it is exposed to water. This helped us understand why the Gingerbread Man might not want to jump into the river!

Last week, our Year 4 children had the exciting opportunity to take part in a virtual space Zoom hosted by STEM with Wings, live from Imperial Space School. The children heard from NASA engineers Howard Hu and Branelle Rodriguez, who shared the incredible story of Artemis II and the team behind the Orion spacecraft.
They learnt about Orion’s 10-day mission around the Moon, including its journey around the far side of the Moon in a figure-of-eight pattern. The children were fascinated to discover that the crew travelled an incredible 270,000 miles from Earth which is farther than any human had travelled since the Apollo missions. It was a fantastic opportunity for our children to hear directly from NASA engineers and learn more about the people and technology behind this historic mission.

They have thoroughly enjoyed creating their own magical worlds, and we have been so impressed by their creativity and imagination. It has been wonderful to see their ideas develop into exciting and imaginative stories!

The new Year 6s have started strong as excellent role models. Not only have they been making a good effort to show their best around the school, but many of them also stood for election as House Captain.
Everyone wrote a speech about why they would be a good leader and then carefully thought about whether they wanted to take on the role and put themselves forward.
It was great to see so many being confident, standing up in front of the members of their house from across the school and seeking election. After some very secret voting across the school, our new house captains were chosen and Mrs Reed presented them with their very special House Captain badges.

02.10.26 Year 6 trip to RAF Museum
The first trip of the year happened on the 22nd of September when Year 6 visited the RAF Museum in Colindale. Their behaviour was exemplary and we received compliments from the staff at the museum who appreciated how well the children listened and moved around the museum. The trip allowed the children to see some of the important aeroplanes from World War Two, particularly from The Battle of Britain. We were met at the museum by a volunteer who made sure we knew where to find everything and then we were free to move around at our leisure. We had a great time looking at the planes and other vehicles at the museum and also enjoyed playing on the interactives, learning a little more about how missions are managed and run. The children also had fun dressing up in the replica uniforms - they really looked the part! We also managed to catch one of the tour guides on a break and persuaded him to answer lots of questions! It was a great day and Year 6 really made Underhill proud.

As we worked, we talked about what plants need to grow and how we can help them by giving them water, soil and sunlight.

Underhill School is a school that loves reading and writing, and our curriculum is designed so the children have a wide range of experiences to develop their communication, reading and writing skills. We teach using the Ready, Steady, Write and Rocket Phonics schemes, and these are supplemented with lots of other exciting activities and learning. You can find out all about our English curriculum below and our English newsletter will tell you lots more about what has been happening at Underhill this year.

Our Phonics Curriculum
Reading
At Underhill School we want our children to love reading and this is at the heart of our reading curriculum. We want all our children to be enthusiastic readers who read widely and frequently and take true pleasure in reading.
You can find out more about how to support children with reading by speaking to your child's class teacher and there's is lots of information on the Reading Planet Parent Hub: https://www.risingstars-uk.com/subjects/parents/parent-hub/reading-with-your-child
Our reading journey starts with systematic teaching of phonics : direct, focused phonics is taught every day in Reception and Key Stage 1. We use a scheme called Rocket Phonics which provides an ambitious framework for teaching of phonics.
As soon as children have learned new sounds, they start to read decodable Target Practice books. They provide focused practice of newly learned sounds and words. We read these fully decodable books as a whole-class, in guided groups , one-to-one and in independent reading.
Guided reading is taught daily. During guided reading the teacher reads with a group of children who all read at the same ability level. Children read a short passage and explore comprehension questions as a group.
We use a reading scheme called Rising Stars: they offer a huge range of books written by experienced educational and children’s writers. All the books have been carefully levelled according to book banding criteria and Lexile measured to ensure steady progression throughout the programme. Children progress through the books until they become a ‘free reader’.
ERICA (Every Child Reading in Class Always)
Every day children read silently for 20 minutes. Children read leveled books from our reading scheme. This is an opportunity for children to progress through the reading scheme and work on their reading speed and fluency and, of course, their love of reading.
FRED (Families Reading Every Day)
We want to work together with our families to improve reading and we encourage children to read at home through our FRED home reading scheme. Every time a child reads for 20 minutes , she or he gets a ‘tick’ which we record in our FRED Reading Diaries.
When we receive 10,000 reads as a school, we celebrate with a whole school reward.
Comprehension lessons
We also have weekly comprehension lessons where children are taught the reading skills and abilities being measured or examined by a test (for example end of KS 1 and end of Key Stage 2 Standard Assessment Tests).
In these lessons children will learn to:
Retrieve and record information
Make comparisons within the text.

ENGLISH AS AN ADDITIONAL LANGUAGE (EAL)
Here at Underhill we are proud to welcome families from a wealth of different cultures and backgrounds and we greatly value the rich diversity of our school community. We have pupils from all around the world and over 45 languages spoken, and as such, support for pupils who are learning English as an additional language is carefully assessed and planned.
Assessment and monitoring
Our pupils new to English are closely monitored for their progress in the curriculum and their acquisition of English. We use an English as an Additional Language (EAL) proficiency assessment framework to track each pupil’s individual progress. This information subsequently informs the EAL support that we put in place for each child.
Provision and resources
We provide support in each class for our EAL pupils at the level they can access, this includes using visuals, translated materials and intervention support to boost vocabulary and communication as required. We use a variety of translated resources across school to support our pupils, including bilingual books, multi-language dictionaries and Google translate.
EAL Buddies
Whenever we have a newly arrived pupil they are buddied up with a classmate in order that they settle into school life and feel welcomed in to Underhill. We also run a peer readers scheme where children from another class will come to read with EAL pupils.
Language of the month
Each month we celebrate and learn about a different language. We warmly welcome any involvement from parents and families and encourage them to get involved, however big or small the contribution.
Bilingual staff
Our staff who speak more than one language read stories to classes in their language to help celebrate diversity.
